title: Paws of Hope: The Storm Under the Red Bridge (S01E01)
hook: For three days, this gentle stray dog guarded an abandoned cardboard box in torrential rain.
script: For three days, this gentle stray dog guarded an abandoned cardboard box in torrential rain. Passersby hurried past in their raincoats, never looking down. Under the iron bridge, Scout curled his wet golden body around a soggy shoebox, refusing to leave. When a railway mechanic finally knelt down with a flashlight, Scout didn't growl. He gently nudged the lid open with his wet nose, revealing a shivering 4-week-old calico kitten. The mechanic carried them both home inside his warm jacket. Today, they sleep together by the fireplace — and Scout still checks on her every two hours.

title: Mochi & Co.: The Health Inspector's Surprise Visit (S01E15)
hook: Barnaby announced a surprise health inspection, and Mochi had 30 seconds to hide the evidence.
script: Barnaby announced a surprise health inspection, and Mochi had 30 seconds to hide the evidence. The brass bell chimed. Barnaby stepped in with his white glove and clipboard, clicking his pen with terrifying precision. Mochi shoved three stolen salmon fillets into Luna's toolbelt, while Pip stood at attention saluting so hard his floppy ears vibrated. Barnaby wiped the top shelf. Barnaby inspected his white glove. Clean. Then Mochi accidentally sneezed a cloud of powdered sugar directly onto Barnaby's shiny black shoes.

title: Through Alternate Eyes: POV: You Are The Last Radio Operator in 2099 (S01E02)
hook: POV: It is midnight in 2099, and your radio antenna just picked up a broadcast from 1944.
script: POV: It is midnight in 2099, and your radio antenna just picked up a broadcast from 1944. Three hundred feet above the sunken ruins of Neo-Tokyo, the aurora borealis hums across the ionosphere while your vacuum tubes crackle. Through eight decades of static, a woman's voice suddenly emerges clear as ice: 'If anyone can hear this from the future, the war ended. Tell us we survived.' You reach for your transmitter switch, hold your breath, and whisper into the cold night: 'You survived. And the stars are still here.'

title: Baby Boss Syndicate: Baby Boss on Morning Naps vs. EBITDA (S01E01)
hook: POV: Your 10-month-old calls an emergency 6 AM meeting to renegotiate nap times.
script: POV: Your 10-month-old calls an emergency 6 AM meeting to renegotiate nap times. Leo adjusted his miniature silk tie, cleared his throat into the studio microphone, and slid the financial charts across the high chair. 'Look team, 2 PM tummy time produces negative ROI. If we swap milk bottles for cold brew and outsource diaper changes to junior analysts, our sleep-adjusted margins double.' He slammed his tiny sippy cup on the desk, stared straight into the lens, and said: 'Sign the pacifier agreement or I cry during your Zoom call with the investors.'

title: Mochi & Co.: The Secret Pizza Midnight Heist (S01E16)
hook: POV: You catch your pets running an illegal underground pizzeria at 2 AM.
script: POV: You catch your pets running an illegal underground pizzeria at 2 AM. At 2:15 AM, the scent of fresh basil and bubbling mozzarella began wafting from the locked pantry door. Behind the flour bags, Mochi had built a miniature brick woodfire oven. Luna was calculating dough hydration on a tiny blackboard while Pip rolled pizza dough with a wine bottle. When the human opened the pantry door, all three froze. Mochi slowly slid a 3-inch truffle pizza across the floor with a note: 'Five stars or we tell the neighbors.'

title: Baby Boss Syndicate: Baby Street Food Mogul: The Pani Puri Empire (S01E02)
hook: Why work corporate when you can make 5,000 dollars a day selling street momos as a toddler?
script: Why work corporate when you can make 5,000 dollars a day selling street momos as a toddler? At 4 PM in Old Delhi, Baby Leo tied his miniature bandana, rolled up his sleeves, and heated up the copper tawa. His tiny hands cracked spiced puris at 180 units per minute. Street vendors twice his age took notes while Leo managed UPI QR codes on his baby monitor. A customer asked for extra spicy chutney. Leo looked him up and down, shook his head, and gave him sweet tamarind: 'You can't handle the heat, my friend. Stick to cerelac.'
